doc.title: Will Shade and Dewey Corley Interview, 1960-05-25

chapter: Beale Street and the early Memphis scene
title: Second reel: Handy, Howard Yancy and other early bandleaders
summary: Back on tape, Shade names bands of his boyhood such as Handy's and Howard Yancy's, and describes the ragtime and Dixieland styles they copied from records.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Okay. Second reel of interview with Will Shade and Dewey Coley. Okay. It's May the 25th, 1960. Thank you. Keep your mic. All right. We were talking about some of the bands they had around here. Do you remember the names of any other ones when you were a little boy?
Oh, W.C. Handy and Howard Yancy, B. Smith. And, uh, oh, quite a few of them. I forgot the name right at the prison. Can't call them right now. So jumped up on me.
How about Howard Yancy? How old was he?
Oh, he was up in the age. He was a man when I was a kid. Knee pants. Oh.
That's the guy right around the corner in the pool room, right? That's right.
He used to have a musician in his headquarters up there. At a club up there. Mm-hmm. I see.
Uh, I see. Uh, now what style of music did you call that that these bands play?

Well, they was playing that ragtime music, you know, and like that, and that Dixieland music down in New Orleans, or like that, way down in New Orleans, all such that. All them old back records that Hannah Beath made, they'd follow behind that, and something else new come out, then they'd read that and pick up on that and learn it, and then they'd play that. Mm-hmm.
